newsitem.title: UK: BT may go to MMC over interconnect price caps.
newsitem.headline: BT may go to MMC over interconnect price caps.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said on Thursday it would consider going to the Monopoly and Mergers Commission if the industry regulator imposes what it calls "unduly harsh" curbs on the prices it charges rivals for carrying calls on its network.

Industry regulator Oftel this week published a consultation document suggesting that a basket of so-called "interconnect" prices should fall by 6-12 percent below the rate of retail price inflation (RPI-6 to RPI-12) from October.
But BT's finance director Robert Brace told reporters after a news conference that even the bottom end of that price cap range may be too much for the company.
"I think RPI-6 would be unduly harsh," he said, noting that the price cap would come on top of a 10-12 percent one-off cut in charges.
BT says the suggested price caps, which represent about one billion stg of its total costs of 12 billion stg, could harm infrastructure investment in Britain.

"(British) interconnect charges are not only the lowest in the world, they are one third of anybody else's," Brace said. "In extremis, we would be prepared to challenge it (the price regime) at the MMC."

Oftel's final proposals will be published in early July. BT, which says it needs a reasonable return on capital, has said it will use the consultative period until June 10 to argue for an acceptable price cap.
